passage: Archaeologists studying a 3,000-year-old village found that its pottery was made from a type of clay that does not occur within 200 kilometers of the site. The pottery shows no signs of having been shaped or fired elsewhere, and unused lumps of the same clay were found in the village's workshops. This evidence suggests that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the villagers brought clay from far away and made the pottery themselves.
the pottery was made in a distant town and then traded to the people of the village.
the clay found near the village has changed over the last 3,000 years.
the village was first settled by potters who came from another region.
steps: The clay came from at least 200 km away.
But the pottery was made locally (no signs of outside shaping, and unused clay in local workshops).
So the villagers transported the clay and made the pots in the village.
Trading finished pots contradicts the workshop evidence; the other choices go beyond the text.
key: Combine all the clues; the right inference is consistent with every one.
